newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania's Renel RA to import 1.3 mlnT fuel oil.
newsitem.headline: Romania's Renel RA to import 1.3 mlnT fuel oil.

text.p: Romanian state-run electricity authority Renel RA will import 1.3 million tonnes of fuel oil for the energy sector this winter, financed by a $160 million syndicated loan it signed on Tuesday, a senior official said.
"These imports will help Romania solve many of its energy problems during the next four winter months," Renel president Victor Romert said.

Romert made the remarks after the signing ceremony of a $160 million syndicated loan, the first by a Romanian corporate, arranged for Renel by ING Bank, with co-arrangers Bank of America NT&SA, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi and BHF-Bank Aktiengesellschaft.

The loan will help Romania avoid a repeat of last winter's energy crisis when an acute hard currency shortage forced the country to drastically reduce its fuel imports. Renel had to cut electricity supplies to most industries over January-March.
Romert said the imports would add to Renel's stocks of some 570,000 tonnes of fuel oil and to some 600,000 tonnes expected to come from local production over the next four months.
He declined to name suppliers for the fuel oil or elaborate on the import terms: "We will go on the international market and buy at the price of the day."
The fuel would be used by Renel to produce electricity and thermal power for the country of 23 million people.
"I can say that Romania is well prepared for this winter," another Renel official said.
Renel has some 6.72 million tonnes of coal stored at thermal power plants across the country, close to the planned level of 7.0 million tonnes, the official said.

Romania's first nuclear power plant built at Cernavoda was also expected to supply some 8.0 percent of Romania's electricity needs "so we are on the safe side", he said. -- Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
